subtype: Approach: skipping the boring chapter and hoping it will not come [Pitfall]
passage: The night before the test, Rajni opened the Civics chapter and closed it again. "So boring," she told her friend Amandeep on the phone. "Ma'am never asks from it." "It might come," said Amandeep. "It won't," said Rajni. She spent the hour on the chapters she liked, and went to bed early. In the exam hall, the last page had a question worth eight marks. It was from Civics. She read it twice and wrote two lines, then stared at the clock. When the paper was returned, she had lost most of those marks, and they were the easy ones.

qa.q: How many marks was the Civics question worth?
What was Rajni feeling when she saw the eight-mark Civics question?
qa.a: She felt shocked and uneasy. She read it twice, wrote only two lines and stared at the clock.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Rajni use for a chapter she dislikes, and why?
qa.a: She could read the chapter in short bursts, picking out the main points first. Then even a boring chapter would not leave big gaps.

qa.q: How might Amandeep see what happened in the exam?
qa.a: Amandeep warned Rajni that it might come, and it did. Amandeep may feel sorry for Rajni but also that the hint was ignored.

grounding: A girl skips the Civics chapter she dislikes and hopes it will not come, but the paper has an eight-mark question on it and she loses easy marks.
